questions.questionText: Table 3 shows indices for the total revenue and total cost for a firm in the years 2021 to 2023, with 2022 set as the base year. In 2021, the firm’s total revenue was £180 000 and its total cost was £160 000. What was the firm’s total profit in 2023?

Using the data in Extract A (Figure 1), calculate how the value of the Norwegian krone has changed compared to the Singapore dollar between 26 October 2021 and 29 May 2023. Give your answer as a percentage and to one decimal place.
Which one of the following is most likely to be an objective of government macroeconomic policy?
options: Achieving deflation in the average price level
Creating a budget surplus during a recession
Generating stable and sustained economic growth
Improving productivity in an electronics firm

questions.questionText: Explain how the data in Extract A (Figure 2) show that Singapore may have benefitted from managing its exchange rate compared to Germany and Norway.
In an economy, the number of people in work is unchanged but the rate of growth of labour productivity slows from 2.3% to 0.4%. It can be concluded that there will be an increase in
options: cyclical unemployment.
national income.
raw material prices.
the negative output gap.

questions.questionText: Extract B (lines 6–7) states: ‘Some analysts hope that, before long, the currency will start to appreciate which could help Norway reduce inflation.’ With the help of a suitable diagram, explain how an appreciation of the krone could help Norway reduce inflation.
In a particular year, the rate of inflation in an economy was 2% and real national income rose by 6%. What was the approximate increase in the economy’s nominal national income in that year?

Extract C (lines 1–2) states: ‘An economy that has seen considerable success by intervening in the foreign exchange market to manage its currency is Singapore.’ Using the data in the extracts and your knowledge of economics, assess the view that an economy is likely to perform better with a managed exchange rate rather than a freely floating exchange rate.

Figure 1 shows the aggregate demand (AD) and long-run aggregate supply (LRAS) curves for an economy. All other things being equal, which one of the following is most likely to cause aggregate demand to shift from AD1 to AD2 and long-run aggregate supply to shift from LRAS1 to LRAS2?
options: A fall in spending on imports and a rise in productivity
A reduction in exports and an increase in imports of capital goods
An increase in Bank Rate and a reduction in firms’ costs of production
An increase in saving and a rise in government spending on infrastructure

questions.questionText: Using the data in Extract D (Figure 3), calculate the difference between the percentage increase in GDP for Japan and the USA between 2001 and 2023. Give your answer to one decimal place.
Which one of the following statements concerning short-run economic growth and long-run economic growth is correct?
options: Short-run growth is inflationary whereas long-run growth will cause a fall in the average price level
Short-run growth may occur independently of the government whereas long-run growth is only achieved as a result of government policy
Short-run growth may occur when governments use demand-side policies but these do not affect long-run growth
Short-run growth may reduce spare capacity whereas long-run growth increases productive capacity

questions.questionText: Explain how the data in Extract D (Figure 3) show how Ethiopia has developed at a faster rate than Japan since 2001.
When an economy goes into a recession, there is most likely to be an increase in
options: business uncertainty.
imports.
inflation.
tax revenue.

questions.questionText: Extract E (lines 15–17) states: ‘In recent years, some of the BRICS+ countries, including China and India, have been responsible for large foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows into the G7.’ With the help of a suitable diagram, explain how increased inward foreign direct investment (FDI) can affect a country’s level of employment.
Table 1 shows the levels of government spending and national income in a country in Year 1 and Year 2. All other things being equal, what is the value of the multiplier to two decimal places?

Extract F (lines 1–2) states: ‘While some see the benefits of the emergence of the BRICS+ economies, others are more worried by their rapid economic growth.’ Using the data in the extracts and your knowledge of economics, assess the view that the continued rapid economic growth of the BRICS+ economies is likely to be damaging to the macroeconomic performance of G7 nations, such as the UK.
Which one of the following is most likely to cause a leftward shift in the short-run aggregate supply curve?
options: A reduction in the national minimum wage
A rise in the general price level
A rise in the price of imported raw materials
An increase in government subsidies to firms

questions.questionText: Explain factors that may lead to an increase in a country’s national debt as a percentage of GDP.
Table 2 shows various macroeconomic indicators for an economy from 2021 to 2023. Which one of the following can be concluded from the data in Table 2?
options: Incomes are more equitably distributed due to lower unemployment
The central bank should reduce interest rates
The government’s budget deficit has increased
There is evidence of a conflict between macroeconomic policy objectives

questions.questionText: Assess the view that raising direct taxes to finance an increase in government spending is better than raising indirect taxes.
Which one of the following combinations consists only of injections into the circular flow of income?
options: Consumption, bank loans, investment
Exports, government spending, investment
Government spending, consumption, exports
Investment, bank loans, exports

questions.questionText: Explain how supply-side policies can help to achieve a low, stable rate of inflation.
Figure 2 shows a production possibility curve for an economy producing consumer and capital goods. The movement from point X to point Y is most likely to have been caused by
options: a fall in the exchange rate.
a fall in the trade surplus.
a rise in the foreign currency price of exports.
a rise in the volume of imports.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the view that a low rate of inflation is always beneficial for a country’s macroeconomic performance.
Which one of the following statements about supply-side policies is correct? Supply-side policies
options: have no effect on aggregate demand.
often rely on creating economic incentives.
only affect long-run aggregate supply.
usually lead to an increase in inflation.

questions.questionText: Explain the main limitations of using national income data to assess differences in living standards between countries.
Which one of the following is the most likely reason for a fall in saving by households?
options: A reduction in consumer confidence
A reduction in income tax rates
An increase in household energy bills
An increase in interest rates

questions.questionText: Assess the view that economic development in LEDCs is best achieved through interventionist strategies.
The textile industry is a major employer of unskilled labour in an economy. The introduction of labour-saving technology in this industry is most likely to lead to an increase in
options: cyclical unemployment.
frictional unemployment.
seasonal unemployment.
structural unemployment.

questions.questionText: To reduce the impact of rising inflation, the government cut indirect taxes on several key goods and services and made a one-off payment to all low-income households. Which one of the following diagrams illustrates the most likely impact on the macroeconomy?
All other things being equal, which one of the following is most likely to reduce the deficit on the UK’s balance of payments on current account?
options: A recovery in the world economy
A rise in the value of the pound
An increase in the price level in the UK
Rising real income levels for UK households

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is most likely to contribute to a decision by the Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Committee to increase Bank Rate?
options: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index
A fall in the number of people applying for mortgages
An increase in the number of job vacancies
Deflation in countries supplying imports to the UK

questions.questionText: Table 3 shows the tax-free allowance and income tax rates in four countries, A, B, C and D. The tax-free allowance is the amount of income on which a person does not pay any income tax. In which country would a person earning $40 000 pay the most income tax?
options: Country A
Country B
Country C
Country D

questions.questionText: According to the accelerator process
options: a fall in the price of capital goods encourages more investment.
an increase in investment leads to a greater increase in national income.
firms invest to increase spare capacity.
investment is determined by past changes in national income.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is most likely to cause a rightward shift in an aggregate demand curve? An increase in
options: indirect taxation.
interest rates.
international competitiveness.
the budget surplus.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following diagrams, A, B, C or D, shows the impact on an economy of a permanent reduction in an indirect tax?
Which one of the following is most likely to lead to an increase in the number of people who are frictionally unemployed in the UK?
options: A fall in the number of Jobcentres provided by the government
A persistent fall in reported levels of consumer confidence
A reduction in the rate at which Jobseeker’s Allowance is paid
A significant real terms increase in the National Living Wage

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is most likely to indicate that a government is trying to cause a significant change in the pattern of economic activity?
options: A reduction in the rate of tax on income from retirement pensions
A reduction in the tax on a good with positive consumption externalities
An increase in the rate of an inheritance tax
An increase in the tax on a good with very inelastic demand

questions.questionText: Which one of the following best explains the operation of the accelerator process?
options: An increase in investment leads to a larger increase in national income
An increase in productive capacity leads to a larger change in investment
The growth of productive capacity depends on the growth in investment
The level of investment depends on the rate of change in national income

questions.questionText: Figure 2 shows the long-run trend rate of unemployment and the actual rate of unemployment in a country over a period of time. At which one of the following points was the economy most likely to be in the recession phase of its economic cycle?
options: Point A
Point B
Point C
Point D

questions.questionText: Table 3 shows the value of the Human Development Index (HDI) for three countries in 2021 and figures from the index’s health and education dimensions. It can be deduced from Table 3 that in 2021
options: Finland had a faster rate of growth than the UK.
Finland’s Human Development Index was 1.1% higher than the UK’s.
Ireland’s gross national income per capita was higher than Finland’s.
Ireland had a more equitable distribution of income than Finland.

questions.questionText: Table 4 shows the index of consumer prices and the unemployment rate for an economy. The data is for the end of each quarter in a particular year. The index of consumer prices for the final quarter of the previous year was 120.9. According to the data, it can be concluded that
options: prices were lower at the start of the year and employment was lower at the end of the year.
the quarterly inflation rate fluctuated whilst the unemployment rate increased throughout the year.
the relationship between the change in the inflation and unemployment rates was positive in each quarter.
there was an inverse relationship between prices and unemployment in each quarter.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is most likely to be included in a broad measure of the money supply but not in a narrow measure of the money supply?
options: Commercial banks’ deposits with the central bank
Notes and coins held by households
Savings deposited with commercial banks that have more than a year to maturity
The total amount owed on credit cards that has been outstanding for more than 28 days

questions.questionText: Table 5 shows the liquidity ratio and capital ratio for two, otherwise identical, banks. All other things being equal, it is likely that
options: Bank Y is less profitable than Bank Z and is less secure.
Bank Y is less profitable than Bank Z but is more secure.
Bank Y is more profitable than Bank Z and is more secure.
Bank Y is more profitable than Bank Z but is less secure.

questions.questionText: Country X and Country Y have identical amounts of the factors of production that can be used to produce either canoes or rowing boats. Figure 7 shows the production possibility frontiers (PPFs) for the two countries. Which one of the following is supported by the data in Figure 7?
options: Country X has both an absolute advantage and a comparative advantage in producing canoes
In Country Y, the production of rowing boats requires two and a half times as many resources as the production of canoes
The maximum number of canoes and rowing boats that Country X and Country Y can produce between them is 400
The opportunity cost of producing a canoe in Country Y is 25% lower than it is in Country X

questions.questionText: Figure 8 shows the domestic demand (Dd) and supply (Sd) curves for paper in a country. Figure 8 also shows the world supply curve when the country does not have any restrictions on imports of paper (Sw) and the world supply curve when a tariff of $10 per unit is imposed on paper imported from the rest of the world (Swt). Following the introduction of the tariff, what is the change in the amount the country has to pay to the rest of the world for the paper it imports?
options: US$2300 million
US$3300 million
US$4050 million
US$5200 million

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a supply-side policy that is most likely to lead to an improvement in the balance of trade in goods and services on the current account of the UK’s balance of payments?
options: A significant and sustained reduction in Bank Rate by the Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of England
Deregulation that makes it easier for UK transnational corporations to invest abroad
Increasing the supply of pounds on the foreign exchange market to reduce the exchange rate and make exports cheaper
Tax breaks for manufacturing firms that invest in upgrading their machinery and other capital goods

questions.questionText: All other things being equal, which one of the following is most likely to be a consequence of inflation in the UK?
options: The amounts outstanding on households’ existing mortgages will fall in real terms
The nominal value of people’s incomes before tax will fall
The price of all goods and services sold in the UK will increase
The real value of the money deposited in commercial banks will increase

questions.questionText: Table 8 shows figures for the population (millions) and GDP ($ billions) of four countries. What is the mean GDP per capita for the four countries?

To what extent, if at all, do the data suggest that the contribution the automotive industry makes to the UK economy has declined significantly since 2015? You must use the data in Extract B to support your assessment.
Explain factors that affect the UK’s balance of trade in motor vehicles.

After considering Extract D, and the original evidence in Extracts A, B and C, would you recommend that the Government continue to subsidise firms to encourage them to set up gigafactories to produce batteries in the UK? Justify your recommendation.
Table 2 shows an index of labour productivity per hour for a large car manufacturer. Which one of the following statements must be true?
options: Output per hour of labour was higher in 2017 than in 2021
